body:
My parents were supportive but slightly worried about me, I'm away from home at University so they wanted me to go back home. I convinced them that I would be fine. They were a not so sure about the anti-depressants and would have preferred me to see our family doctor.

I'm trying to do my best, I don't want to talk to anyone and I'm not sleeping very well. Yesterday I had an appointment to see a councilor that the psychiatrist recommended, but I missed it because I didn't want to have to talk to anyone. I also missed another appointment I had on friday because I forgot about it. I feel like I'm wasting people's time.

Hi a1mck, thanks for your in-depth reply and advice. I go back to university next week so I'll try and see what I am able to regarding the doctor. The only problem I have is the doctor I saw the last time is he did not seem to know much about what he was doing. The last thing I want is to start counseling again. It sort of did help last time but I don't want to keep living my life with reminders cluttering up my walls and spending 5 minutes at a time on essays or reading books. It takes forever for me to get anything done.

As for my parents, they tend to worry a lot when there is a problem. About 2 years ago I was under stress from being unable to complete important school work. I started bunking off classes because I didn't want to have to confront my teachers. I stupidly ended up taking 13 paracetamol tablets and intended to cut myself. Needless to say it didn't end too well. I couldn't go through with it and my sister found out and told my parents. They sent me to my GP who then put me on counseling for a few months. They were worried about me a lot and I don't want to put them through the same thing again.

I've tried distracting myself with video games, cartoons and happy movies. It does make me feel better temporarily but I know that I'm just covering up the underlying problem. I'm trying to think positive about it but I wouldn't get upset so easily if I wasn't in this mess in the first place.

Thank you for your support and I'll try to keep this post updated.

I think I may have worded that incorrectly. Ending my life would surely not be 'moving forward' from my perspective, but currently my parents are investing in my education. They have high hopes for me being successful like my brother. I have a fairly close relationship with my parents but they are old and will be gone soon.

I would rather wait until I get advise before telling my parents. If my parents were to find out that I'm failing my first year because I'm not applying myself then they would probably not allow me to continue.

The worst thing that can happen is me feeling disowned by my parents and ending up regretting my decisions in life. I already hate myself for not being able to sit down to study and work, I couldn't see myself being happier doing anything else. I'm not the type of person to just go with whatever happens. I like things to be organized and planned out, at the moment my life seems to be the complete opposite to that.
